articles.author: Vijay Kumar
articles.description:
While sharing Stoqyy publicly, one response stood out to me today:
“This is something I might very much need.”
That single line validated why I started building this product.
Stoqyy exists because many small businesses still manage:
Sales in one app
Inventory in notebooks or spreadsheets
Profits by gut feeling
As developers, it’s easy to over-engineer solutions. But building Stoqyy has been about doing the opposite—reducing cognitive load.
Every decision in Stoqyy comes back to one question:
Can a business owner understand their situation in seconds?
From a technical standpoint, that means:
Fewer UI states
Clear data models
Real-time but calm dashboards
Performance that works on low-end devices
Sharing early helps surface real-world feedback faster than assumptions ever could. Comments like today’s aren’t about validation—they’re about direction.
They tell me I’m working on a real pain, not an imagined one.
Still refining flows.
If you’re curious, you can see what I’m building here:
https://stoqyy.com
More updates soon—shipping, breaking, learning.
articles.title: Building Stoqyy in Public

If you have spent more than a week architecting solutions on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), you have likely stared at the metadata inputs for a resource and felt a twinge of confusion. You see a field for Labels. You see a field for Tags.
To the uninitiated, these are synonyms. In almost every other context in the software engineering world, a label and a tag are the same thing. They are key-value pairs used to categorize an object for searchability.
But in GCP, treating them as synonyms is an architectural trap that can lead to security holes, billing nightmares, and governance failures. While they share a similar syntax (key:value), they represent two completely different philosophical approaches to cloud governance. One is a Post-it note. The other is a security badge.
